prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere products, predictable latency, documented quality). External: spacecraft, launch segment, user processing environments, conjunction data source. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time authority, pass supervision, anomaly response, owns contact schedule, routing policy, command engineering (gets command prep package from Mission Planning System); contacts: readiness check, monitoring, closure; sends constraints to MPS; coordinates mode/priority changes with PPF; requires flight dynamics deliveries to state validity interval, frame, generation time, use. Command approval needs MCC + Spacecraft Operations Team concurrence before uplink queueing. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): validates command stacks (syntax, timing, ranges, mode, baseline, maneuver parameters vs screened burn plan); rejects unapproved edits, missing provenance, expired configs, out-of-window items. Cybersecurity Desk reviews prep exceptions. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): authoritative orbit catalog; sends ephemerides/event predictions via controlled interfaces to MCC, MPS, PPF; antenna pointing, attitude geometry, Star Tracker Mask File. Flight Dynamics Team: uses Doppler Residual Report; maneuver/collision screening; sends maneuver recommendation package to Spacecraft Operations Team (with lead time to rehearse, verify contingencies, coordinate coverage); produces Ephemeris Delta Note when state updates shift acquisition times/geometry beyond thresholds. Orbit Determination Engine: fits orbit from North/South S-Band, Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band tracking; produces Doppler Residual Report, Laser Retroreflector Window. Product Quality Service checks orbit solutions. MPS (Cedar): authoritative timeline; aligns requests, contacts, recorder margins, downlinks using accepted orbit files. Network Control System (Lantern): WAN, station allocation, link config, timing; prepares contacts from pointing predictions. Payload Calibration Team uses predicted geometry. Long Term Archive retains orbit products, covariance, maneuver records, quality decisions. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): telemetry to traceable image products; Primary Processing Cluster (L0: deframe, order packets, keep time tags; L1A reconstruct samples+engineering context; L1B radiometric calibration; L2 geolocation, atmospheric screening, gridding); Backup Processing Cluster takes over with same checks/rules. Station delivery files+manifest verified (size, sequence, checksum, acquisition time). Telemetry Ingest Service: writes to immutable staging, records session ID, Pass Replay Packet; corrupt segments isolated (recover/retransmit/discard). Ground Network Manager.

New part:
S158: Each processing level records software build identifiers, calibration baseline identifiers, and ancillary input versions so that a product can be regenerated under audit.
S159: The Long Term Archive is also known as Granite in operator procedures for storage capacity and retrieval coordination.
S160: Released products are stored in the Long Term Archive with metadata that distinguish operational output from test output and reprocessed output.
S161: The Payload Calibration Team maintains the approved calibration baseline and reviews trend evidence before a new baseline is made eligible for operational use.
S162: The Product Quality Service uses the patch bundle to update calibration applicability checks before the next product assessment cycle.
S163: Calibration changes are first applied to a controlled sample of recent scenes, and the resulting metrics are compared with the current operational baseline.
S164: If a calibration change alters radiometric scale, geometric alignment, or saturation behavior, affected product specifications are updated before general release resumes.
S165: The Product Quality Service assigns quality flags for missing source packets, timing discontinuity, saturation, cloud screening uncertainty, geolocation residuals, and processing fallback.
S166: Quality flags are encoded in product metadata and summary records so that automated consumers can reject, warn, or accept data consistently.
S167: A product is placed in a delivery hold state when mandatory checks fail, required ancillary data are missing, or an operator opens a blocking review.
S168: The Product Quality Service produces the Product Hold List when release blocking defects must be tracked across scenes and processing levels.
S169: Held products remain reproducible in staging storage, but they are not promoted for user delivery until the blocking condition has been cleared.
S170: The Network Control System uses the Security Exception Ticket to restrict affected transfer paths until approved containment actions are complete.
S171: Lantern shall preserve the last validated routing configuration and reject unreviewed changes while payload product transfers are active.
S172: When the Primary Processing Cluster cannot meet the processing window, the scheduling service assigns eligible jobs to the Backup Processing Cluster using the same container image and rule set.
S173: The Backup Processing Cluster writes provenance that identifies the fallback execution path, and the Product Quality Service treats that marker as an input to its quality decision.
S174: The Long Term Archive sends the Storage Watermark Snapshot after each daily storage assessment.
S175: If both clusters are unavailable, processing is suspended, raw data are preserved in staging, and Mission Control Center is notified through the normal operational event channel.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.

Command uplink needs MCC + Spacecraft Operations Team concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey) validates command stacks (syntax, timing, ranges, mode, baseline, burn plan); rejects unapproved/unprovenanced/expired/out-of-window items.
